subject: Follow-up: ClearPath prompt intake and regression guardrails
messages:
From: Sana Malik <sana@clearpath.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Reed <oliver@clearpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap + initial prompt batch timeline

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the product team appreciated how Redwood handled long-context Q&A and the live latency numbers. A quick recap from our side and what we can deliver next: 

- Priority need: Accurate extraction of financial line items from multi-page invoices + conversational clarification when data is ambiguous.
- Regulatory note: Some invoices can include customer SSNs or bank details; we need a clear redaction workflow before any data leaves our systems.
- Next deliverable from ClearPath: export of ~1k representative user prompts/examples (customer queries, multi-turn clarifications, and the trickier edge cases) by end of week.

Can you confirm the format you prefer (CSV columns, example labels) and any automated redaction steps you recommend so we don’t accidentally include PII in the sample export? Oliver and I can assemble the export; we wanted to align on the column set first.

Thanks,
Sana Malik
Product Manager — ClearPath Analytics

--
Attachment: will attach sample export once we confirm format (we may send as multiple batches)

From: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + initial prompt batch timeline

Hi Sana — great to meet the team today. Appreciated the clear product context. Short answers and an action plan: 

1) Preferred sample format
- CSV with columns: prompt_id, user_query, prior_turns (pipe-separated), expected_label/intents, gold_response (if available), sensitivity_flags (free text).
- If including attachments/text from invoices, include a redaction_status column (raw | redacted | withheld).

2) Redaction guidance (quick):
- Prefer that ClearPath remove or mask full SSNs/IBANs and full bank account numbers prior to the sample export. If you can’t, mark rows with sensitivity_flags=PII and set redaction_status=raw so we can arrange a secure transfer.

3) Recommended model starting points (based on workload):
- redwood-13b-std: best balance for extraction accuracy on multi-sentence inputs.
- redwood-7b-highmem: lower cost with good structured-extract performance on short invoices.
- redwood-3b-quant: for high-volume use-cases where latency and cost matter; good for intent detection but expect lower extraction fidelity.

4) Benchmarks / eval plan we’ll run (we’ll seed these once we have your sample):
- Basic metrics: field-level precision/recall, intent classification accuracy.
- Safety/regression: hallucination rate on fields that require numeric fidelity, and false disclosure rate for PII.

Action items for this thread:
- Sana / Oliver: share the CSV (see format above). If redaction is a blocker, attach a compliance note and mark rows with sensitivity_flags.
- Ben: can you link the preliminary benchmark rubric in this thread?
- Marissa: will propose a quick eval slate (2k prompts) and expected SLOs.

If it helps, here’s a short benchmarks folder — we’ll populate a model/sequence-length matrix after we see the samples: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3-example-benchmarks

— Hiro Tanaka
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Sana Malik <sana@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 18:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + initial prompt batch timeline

Hi Sana — adding the evaluation plan and a redaction checklist you can use to prep the CSV.

Quick eval slate we recommend (will run once samples arrive):
- Dataset size: 2k prompt/responses drawn from your 1k export + synthesized edgecases we capture with you.
- Acceptance thresholds (proposed): intent accuracy >= 88%, field extraction F1 >= 0.80, hallucination rate <= 4% on numeric fields.
- Regression monitoring: we’ll run model A/B between redwood-13b-std and redwood-7b-highmem and flag any >5% drop in extraction F1.

Redaction checklist (examples to remove/mask before upload):
- Full SSNs (xxx-xx-xxxx) -> mask to XXX-XX-1234 or remove field.
- Full bank account numbers and IBANs -> remove or replace with [BANK_ACCT_REMOVED].
- Full card PANs -> remove or mask to **** **** **** 1234.
- Customer names are OK if already pseudonymized; otherwise mark sensitivity_flags=customer_name.

File format reminder: UTF-8 CSV, no embedded images. If you must include raw PDFs, set redaction_status=raw and we will coordinate a secure transfer (S3 with encryption).

I’ve also started a shared results sheet where we’ll publish the benchmark runs and regression alerts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB3-example-benchmarks

Finally — two asks for ClearPath to make the bench useful:
1) Please include 200 examples where the invoice data is intentionally ambiguous (e.g., "line item 3 could be tax vs service") so we can measure clarification-turn behavior.
2) Flag any rows where legal/regulatory review is required. We’ll exclude those from public dashboards but will evaluate in a secure workspace.

Once we have the CSV I’ll schedule the initial 2k run and tag the results to DEAL-4921 in our HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/4921

— Marissa Cole
Senior ML Ops | Redwood Inference

Attachments: redaction_checklist.md (text), eval_rubric_preview.pdf

From: Sana Malik <sana@clearpath.ai>
To: Hiro Tanaka <hiro.tanaka@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + initial prompt batch timeline

Thanks — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. Oliver and I will produce the CSV in the format you outlined and (1) mask SSNs to XXX-XX-1234, (2) replace full bank account numbers with [BANK_ACCT_REMOVED], and (3) flag sensitive rows with sensitivity_flags and redaction_status=raw where applicable.

We’ll upload two files to you by Tue 2027-06-10: clearpath_prompts_batch.csv and a short compliance note (clearpath_compliance_note.pdf) explaining internal controls on the data export. If you need the data transferred via a secure S3 link instead of email/Drive, let us know and we’ll coordinate.

One quick question: for the 200 ambiguity examples Marissa requested, do you want us to include the human follow-up annotation (i.e., expected next-user-turn) or should we only supply the ambiguous prompt and let Redwood synthesize the follow-up?

We can do either — prefer to confirm so we don’t over-annotate.

Best,
Sana Malik
Product Manager — ClearPath Analytics

Attachment: clearpath_compliance_note.pdf
